relationships.subject: LH PV to vlPAG pathway
relationships.evidence_quote: In two models of persistent pain, optogenetic activation of LH<sup>PV</sup> neurons or their ventrolateral periaqueductal gray area (vlPAG) axonal projections attenuates nociception

relationships.subject: LH PV neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Together, these results indicate that LHPV neuronal activation attenuates hypersensitivity to both thermal and mechanical stimuli following the onset of inflammation.

relationships.subject: LH PV neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: neuroanatomical tracing reveals that LH<sup>PV</sup> neurons preferentially target glutamatergic over GABAergic neurons in the vlPAG

relationships.subject: LH PV to LHb pathway
relationships.evidence_quote: By contrast, LH<sup>PV</sup> projections to the lateral habenula regulate aversion but not nociception.

relationships.subject: LH PV neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Thus, activating LHPV neurons not only increases morphine potency acutely but also rescues morphine tolerance and may prevent subsequent tolerance development.

relationships.subject: LH LEPR to vlPAG pathway
relationships.evidence_quote: we found that activation of the LHLEPR→vlPAG pathway potentiated both thermal and mechanical nociception in healthy mice

key_findings: Activation of LH parvalbumin glutamatergic neurons or their vlPAG projections attenuated nociception in inflammatory and neuropathic pain models; LHPV preferentially target vlPAG glutamatergic neurons.
LHPV activation synergized with morphine and restored morphine antinociception after tolerance; LHPV-to-LHb projections mediate aversion, not nociception.
